title: Scaffold ccw bash CLI with help and argument parsing
description:
Create the `agents/cli/ccw` bash script skeleton with:
- `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail`
- Top-level subcommand dispatch (`case "$1" in start|list|status|ssh|shell|logs|stop|dismiss|dismiss-all|help)`
- `ccw help` / `ccw --help` showing all subcommands with brief descriptions
- Common helper functions:
  - `CCW_NAMESPACE=claude-workers`
  - `pod_name <task>` — validates task exists as a pod
  - `require_task <task>` — exits with error if pod not found
  - `get_pod_label <pod> <label>` — extracts a label value via jsonpath
  - `find_pod_template` — locates pod-template.yaml relative to script or via `$CCW_POD_TEMPLATE`
- `agents/cli/install.sh` that copies `ccw` to `~/.local/bin/ccw` and makes it executable
acceptance_criteria: `ccw help` prints usage without errors
`ccw` with no args prints help
`ccw unknown-command` prints error and help
`bash agents/cli/install.sh` installs ccw to ~/.local/bin/ccw
Script has no shellcheck warnings

title: Implement `ccw start`
description:
Implement the `ccw start` subcommand.

Arguments:
- `--repo <url>` (required) — git repository URL
- `--branch <name>` (required) — branch to work on (created if not exists)
- `--prompt <text>` (required) — initial prompt for Claude
- `--ticket <id>` (optional, default: none) — Linear ticket ID
- `--image <image>` (optional) — override container image

Behavior:
1. Validate required args
2. Generate task name: `<repo-slug>-<yyyymmdd>-<4-char-random>` (max 63 chars)
3. Extract repo slug from URL for labels (URL-encode slashes as hyphens)
4. Write the prompt to a temp file (to handle special chars safely)
5. Export env vars: TASK_NAME, REPO_URL, REPO_SLUG, GIT_BRANCH, LINEAR_TICKET, CLAUDE_IMAGE
6. Run `envsubst < <pod-template> | kubectl apply -f -`
7. Print task name and connection instructions:
   ```
   Task started: my-app-20240315-a3f9
   To connect:   ccw ssh my-app-20240315-a3f9
   To monitor:   ccw logs my-app-20240315-a3f9 --follow
   ```
acceptance_criteria: `ccw start --repo <url> --branch main --prompt 'list files'` creates a pod in claude-workers
Pod has correct labels: app, task, repo, branch, ticket, status=running
Task name is printed after creation
Error if --repo, --branch, or --prompt are missing
Long repo names are truncated so pod name stays under 63 chars

title: Implement `ccw list`
description:
Implement `ccw list` to show all worker pods in a human-readable table.

Use `kubectl get pods -n claude-workers -l app=claude-worker` with `-o custom-columns` or pipe through `jq` for formatting.

Output columns:
- TASK (pod name)
- STATUS (from label `status`, not pod phase)
- REPO (from label `repo`)
- BRANCH (from label `branch`)
- TICKET (from label `ticket`, omit if none)
- AGE (from pod creation timestamp, formatted as Xm/Xh/Xd)
- NODE

Color-code STATUS:
- `running` → green
- `done` → dim/grey
- `error` → red
- `rate-limited` → yellow
- `queued` → blue

(Use tput colors if terminal supports it, plain text otherwise.)
acceptance_criteria: `ccw list` shows all claude-worker pods in a table
STATUS column shows the pod label value (not Kubernetes pod phase)
Output is readable in a standard terminal column width
Works when there are zero pods (prints header + empty state message)
Color codes are skipped when output is piped (not a TTY)

title: Implement `ccw status <task>`
description:
Implement `ccw status <task>` to show detailed information about a single task.

Output:
```
Task:     my-app-20240315-a3f9
Status:   running
Repo:     https://github.com/user/my-app
Branch:   feat/login
Ticket:   LIN-234
Node:     beelink2
Age:      14m
Pod IP:   10.42.1.15

--- Recent output (last 30 lines) ---
<tail of /workspace/.claude-output.log via kubectl exec>
```

Fetch pod metadata via `kubectl get pod -n claude-workers <task> -o json` + jq.
Fetch recent output via `kubectl exec -n claude-workers <task> -- tail -n 30 /workspace/.claude-output.log`.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw status <task>` shows all metadata fields
Recent output section shows last 30 lines of Claude's output log
Error message if task doesn't exist
Output section is skipped gracefully if log file doesn't exist yet

title: Implement `ccw ssh` and `ccw shell`
description:
Implement two connection subcommands:

`ccw ssh <task>` — attaches to the Claude tmux session:
```bash
kubectl exec -it -n claude-workers <pod> -- tmux attach -t claude
```
If Claude is done and tmux session no longer exists, print a message and offer to open a shell instead.

`ccw shell <task>` — opens a plain bash shell in the pod:
```bash
kubectl exec -it -n claude-workers <pod> -- bash
```

Both commands should print a brief reminder before connecting:
- For ssh: "Attaching to Claude's tmux session. Detach with Ctrl+B D."
- For shell: "Opening bash shell. Claude is running in tmux session 'claude'."
acceptance_criteria: `ccw ssh <task>` attaches to the tmux session named `claude`
`ccw shell <task>` opens a bash shell
Helpful message is printed before connecting
Graceful error if pod doesn't exist
`ccw ssh` prints helpful message if tmux session doesn't exist (Claude already finished)

title: Implement `ccw logs <task>`
description:
Implement `ccw logs <task> [--follow]` to read Claude's output log from the pod.

The log is at `/workspace/.claude-output.log` inside the pod.

Without `--follow`: print last 100 lines via `kubectl exec -- tail -n 100`.
With `--follow`: stream the log live via `kubectl exec -- tail -f`.

Also support `ccw logs <task> --since <N>` to show last N lines.

Note: this is different from `kubectl logs <pod>` which shows container stdout. This reads the Claude-specific output log that the entrypoint tees.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw logs <task>` prints last 100 lines of Claude's output
`ccw logs <task> --follow` streams new output as it arrives
`ccw logs <task> --since 50` shows last 50 lines
Graceful error if pod or log file doesn't exist

title: Implement `ccw stop` and `ccw dismiss`
description:
Implement two lifecycle subcommands:

`ccw stop <task>` — gracefully stops Claude but keeps the pod alive:
```bash
# Send SIGTERM to Claude process inside pod
kubectl exec -n claude-workers <pod> -- pkill -SIGTERM -f 'claude'
# Update status label
kubectl label pod -n claude-workers <pod> status=stopped --overwrite
```
Print: "Claude stopped. Pod is still running. Use `ccw dismiss <task>` to remove it."

`ccw dismiss <task>` — deletes the pod entirely:
```bash
kubectl delete pod -n claude-workers <pod>
```
Confirm before deleting if pod status is `running` (prompt: "Task is still running. Dismiss anyway? [y/N]")

`ccw dismiss-all` — dismiss all pods with `status=done` or `status=error`. Require explicit `--include-running` flag to dismiss running pods.

`ccw stop-all` — stop Claude in all `status=running` pods.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw stop <task>` sends SIGTERM to Claude, updates label to stopped
`ccw dismiss <task>` deletes the pod
`ccw dismiss <task>` prompts for confirmation when pod is running
`ccw dismiss-all` removes done/error pods without confirmation
`ccw dismiss-all --include-running` also removes running pods with confirmation
